extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of media sociology, media effects researchers, journalism/media studies instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Using the Hierarchy of Influences theoretical framework to analyze and evaluate media content, from broad social systems down to individual-level factors; intended as a textbook guide for students and researchers in media sociology and journalism studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Hierarchical Model
rubrics_metrics.description: An updated Hierarchy of Influences Model that ranges from ideological to individual levels of analysis and works with traditional and 'new' communication professions alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hierarchical model to structure analysis of media content by tracing influences at multiple levels (ideological/social systems → institutions → organizations → routines → individuals). The model 'guides readers toward systematic theoretical thinking about the creation of media content.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Shaping Social Reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination of how media content constructs and represents social reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the ways messages shape audiences' perceptions and representations of events, groups, and issues; consider framing and representational effects as part of media sociology analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual-level influences on media content (e.g., personal attributes, beliefs, decisions of media professionals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how journalists' and producers' backgrounds, orientations, and choices affect content selection and presentation; account for micro-level motivations and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The routine practices of news/media production that shape content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze production routines, gatekeeping processes, newsroom procedures, and standard operating practices that systematically influence what becomes news and how it is presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational-level factors (ownership, managerial policies, economic structures) influencing media content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider organizational structure, editorial policies, commercial pressures, and strategic imperatives when evaluating why content looks the way it does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of social institutions in shaping media content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine influences from institutions such as politics, law, education, and religion that set contexts and constraints for media production and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader societal and ideological systems that condition media messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cultural norms, dominant ideologies, power relations, and macro-level social forces that shape the range and form of media content across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing Media Sociology Hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches to empirically testing hypotheses derived from media sociology theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply rigorous empirical methods to test theoretical propositions about media influences; prioritize methodological clarity and hypothesis-driven research when assessing claims about media effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Sociology Theories in the 21st Century
rubrics_metrics.description: Updating and applying media sociology theories to contemporary media environments (including entertainment media and the Internet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess theoretical frameworks for their applicability to new media technologies and entertainment-focused content; ensure theories account for Internet-era practices and professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Entertainment Media and the Internet
rubrics_metrics.description: An added emphasis in the new edition on entertainment media and the Internet as important influences on media content in the twenty-first century.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating media messages, include analysis of entertainment industries, online platforms, and digital distribution mechanisms as distinct and influential forces shaping content.
